title: GA Launch Brief (Draft) — Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode
content:
Doc purpose
This is the GA launch brief for Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds (min/max) and Predictive Autoscaling Mode. It is intended for internal alignment across Product, Eng, SRE, CS/Support, Sales/TAM, and Solutions.

Status / TL;DR
- What’s launching: Customer-configurable autoscaling bounds for Dedicated deployments (hard min/max) + optional predictive scaling input that biases scale decisions while always respecting bounds.
- Why it matters: Enterprise Dedicated customers want explicit spend ceilings and guaranteed baseline capacity; predictable daily ramps currently cause queueing/latency and customer escalations.
- Launch approach: Feature-flagged rollout (per account/deployment), canary by region, then GA for Dedicated accounts with guardrails + documented semantics.

Proposed GA date + scope
- Target GA window: Week of 2025-09-08 (subject to go/no-go)
- Regions: us-east-1 + eu-west-1 in week 1; expand to remaining Dedicated regions in week 2 if no regressions.
- Accounts: GA-eligible Dedicated accounts. Predictive mode remains opt-in and gated by “predictive_autoscaling” flag; bounds can be enabled separately.

What’s included (customer-facing)
1) Autoscaling bounds (GA)
- Per Dedicated deployment, customers can configure:
  - min_replicas (hard floor; autoscaler must not scale below)
  - max_replicas (hard ceiling; autoscaler must not scale above)
  - scale_up_cooldown / scale_down_cooldown (guardrails)
- Semantics:
  - Autoscaler computes a “requested desired” from signals.
  - We clamp to bounds to produce “bounded desired”.
  - We emit metrics + audit events capturing both values and decision reasons.
- Backward compatibility:
  - Existing deployments retain current behavior until bounds are explicitly configured/enabled.

2) Predictive scaling mode (GA as “Available” but recommended “Pilot/Guided” messaging)
- Optional forecast-based bias signal (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events, historical rates/latency).
- Reactive saturation/queue signals can override predictive bias when prediction is wrong.
- Always respects bounds.
- Fallback behavior:
  - If forecast is stale/unavailable: fall back to reactive-only behavior (and never scale-to-zero due to null predictions; see hotfix).

What’s NOT included / non-goals
- Cross-region active-active placement optimization.
- Automated procurement / contract renegotiation flows.
- Fully autonomous scaling without any reactive safeguards.

Target personas + primary use cases
- Platform/Infra owners (enterprise): “I need a hard max to prevent runaway spend and a hard min to guarantee baseline throughput.”
- App teams with predictable ramps: “Every day at 9am local time we ramp 3–4x; reactive scaling is late and we queue.”
- Compliance-heavy customers: “I need auditability of scaling policy changes and why the system scaled.”

Customer messaging (external)
Positioning statement (short)
“Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds let you set hard minimum and maximum capacity for your Dedicated deployments, giving you a guaranteed baseline for performance and a clear ceiling for spend. For predictable traffic ramps, Predictive Mode can proactively scale up ahead of demand—while still honoring your bounds.”

What customers get (bullets for release notes / email)
- Control costs with a hard max replica bound (prevents unexpected scale-up).
- Protect latency/SLOs with a hard min replica bound (prevents scaling below your safe baseline).
- Improve ramp performance with optional predictive scaling (proactive scale-up based on expected demand).
- Better transparency via dashboards + audit logs (see desired vs bounded capacity and scaling decision reasons).

Messaging guidance / caveats
- Bounds are hard invariants, but min bound may be temporarily unmet if the region is capacity constrained. In that scenario, we surface a degraded state and alert; we do not silently violate max.
- Predictive mode is safe by default (falls back to reactive; cooldown and anti-oscillation included), but we will message it as “recommended with Redwood guidance” for the first 2–4 weeks post-GA while we monitor across more diverse workloads.

Customer FAQ (draft)
Q: If I set max_replicas, will Redwood ever exceed it to protect latency?
A: No. Max is a hard ceiling. If you hit max and traffic exceeds capacity, you may see queueing/latency. We provide alerts and dashboards to help you detect when max is constraining.

Q: If I set min_replicas, is it guaranteed?
A: The autoscaler will never intentionally scale below min. However, if the region cannot provision the requested capacity (e.g., temporary GPU shortage), your deployment can be in a “min_unmet” degraded state. We alert and continue retrying with backoff.

Q: Can predictive mode scale me up too early and waste spend?
A: Predictive mode biases desired capacity upward ahead of demand. We cap by max, apply cooldown/dampening, and revert to reactive behavior if predictions are stale/unavailable. We also expose prediction vs actual error so you can tune.

Q: How do I choose min/max?
A: Start from baseline throughput requirements (min) + budget ceiling (max). Redwood Console shows recommended ranges based on recent utilization; CS/TAM can assist with sizing for SLOs.

Enablement checklist (internal)
Product + Docs
- [ ] Customer docs updated (how to set min/max; semantics; troubleshooting)
- [ ] Release notes entry drafted and approved
- [ ] Console copy: field descriptions, warnings (min > max), and “recommended range” messaging
- [ ] CS playbook published: “Questions to ask”, interpretation of bound-hit metrics, misconfig patterns

Engineering + SRE readiness
- [ ] Feature flags verified: per-account and per-deployment gating
- [ ] Migration/backfill validated: no behavior changes until opt-in
- [ ] Audit events enabled and retention confirmed for enterprise accounts
- [ ] Dashboards shipped: desired vs bounded replicas; bound-hit rate; queue depth; prediction error
- [ ] Alerts shipped and tested:
  - sustained max-bound saturation + queue buildup
  - min_unmet degraded state (capacity shortage)
  - prediction pipeline outage / forecast staleness (only if predictive enabled)
- [ ] Runbook complete and on-call reviewed (safe mitigations + escalation paths)
- [ ] Game day completed for forecast outage and traffic ramp scenarios

GTM (Sales/TAM/CS)
- [ ] Internal one-pager for AEs/TAMs: what it is, who it’s for, how to request enablement
- [ ] Support macros prepared (bounded scaling explanation; next-step questions; recommended mitigations)
- [ ] Pilot to GA transition comms drafted for existing pilot customers

Internal communications plan
Primary channels
- #product (announce GA scope, link docs, enablement process)
- #sales + #cs (what’s new, qualification questions, “when to use bounds vs predictive”)
- #eng-sre + #eng-infra (monitoring focus for first 2 weeks; escalation expectations)

Announcement content (template)
Subject: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds now GA (+ Predictive Mode available)
Body:
- Customer value: hard spend ceilings + baseline throughput
- How to enable: Console per-deployment settings (or request enablement if account-gated)
- Where to monitor: Grafana dashboard link + key metrics
- Known caveats: min_unmet on regional shortages; predictive is opt-in and should be rolled out gradually
- Escalation: Support/SRE runbook link + who to page

Customer communication plan
Segments
1) Existing Dedicated customers (general)
- Email + release notes: bounds GA, how to configure, safety semantics.
- CTA: set max to match budget ceiling; set min to protect known baseline.

2) Customers with prior escalations around spend caps / queueing ramps
- Targeted outreach from CS/TAM:
  - SUP-28411 cohort: “max bound prevents runaway scale”
  - SUP-28437 cohort: “predictive mode for daily ramp; propose gradual enablement”

3) Pilot customers currently running predictive
- Close the loop on pilot outcomes; confirm stable config; ask for permission to use anonymized quote if applicable.

Enablement / rollout mechanics
- Default: bounds + predictive features are present but disabled by default for existing deployments until explicitly configured.
- Account gating:
  - bounds: allow self-serve after GA (unless contract exceptions)
  - predictive: keep gated for 2–4 weeks; enable via internal request + checklist (traffic pattern suitability, monitoring set up)
- Recommendation: roll out per deployment (start with one non-critical deployment) before broad enablement.

Post-launch monitoring plan (first 14 days)
Daily checklist (SRE + Product)
- Monitor bound-hit rate distribution (are many customers immediately clamped by max?)
- Monitor queue depth / latency regressions correlated with max-bound saturation
- Monitor min_unmet occurrences by region (capacity shortage signals)
- Monitor scale event frequency (oscillation detection)
- For predictive-enabled deployments:
  - prediction error metrics (forecast vs actual)
  - incidence of fallback to reactive (forecast staleness/outage)

Dashboards / metrics to watch (high-level)
- desired_replicas_requested vs desired_replicas_bounded
- bound_hit_total (max_hit / min_hit counters)
- queue_depth, request_wait_time, p95/p99 latency by deployment
- saturation signals (GPU utilization, KV cache pressure where applicable)
- scale_event_count by reason (reactive, predictive, bounded, cooldown)
- predictive_error (MAPE or equivalent), forecast_staleness_seconds

Alert response / escalation (first 2 weeks)
- Paging thresholds tuned conservatively at GA (avoid noise; bias towards catching max-bound + queue growth issues).
- Escalate to:
  - Fleet Autoscaling: Vanessa Ortiz / Keiko Yamamoto for autoscaler logic issues
  - Control Plane API/Validation: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor for config or RBAC issues
  - Observability: Allison Grant / Sergio Costa for dashboard/alert issues
  - Support: Dev Patel for customer comms and ticket routing

Go/no-go criteria (for GA announcement)
Must-have
- Bounds enforcement verified in at least one canary region with no regressions
- Audit events present for policy changes and scaling decisions
- Dashboards available and validated by SRE
- Runbook reviewed and linked in on-call rotation docs
- Docs + release notes ready

Should-have
- Predictive fallback behavior validated under forecast outage
- Rate limiting on config churn enabled (prevents thrash)
- Terraform support staged (if not GA day 1, provide timeline)

Known risks + mitigations
1) Risk: Customers set max too low, hit max, then experience queueing and blame platform.
Mitigation: Console warning + “recommended range” + alerting + CS playbook for sizing conversations.

2) Risk: Customers set min too high, increasing regional capacity pressure and causing min_unmet for others.
Mitigation: Validation + policy guidance + internal capacity review for unusually high mins; degraded state surfaced; proactive comms during shortages.

3) Risk: Predictive mode causes oscillation on spiky workloads.
Mitigation: Cooldowns/dampening + minimum step sizing + keep predictive gated; recommend enablement only for strong periodicity initially.

4) Risk: Misinterpretation of “hard min” during shortage events.
Mitigation: Clear semantics in docs: “never intentionally scale below min; may be temporarily unmet if capacity cannot be provisioned”; add UI state + alert.

Open items (as of last edit)
- Confirm final GA date after final readiness review (Priya + Neha sign-off)
- Confirm whether predictive mode is labeled “GA” vs “GA (Guided)” in Console
- Finalize support macros and link them from the playbook
- Confirm Terraform ETA and whether it’s included in GA comms or as a follow-up

Owner / approvals
- DRI: Lauren Bishop (Product)
- Program coordination: Talia Benson
- Eng leads: Vanessa Ortiz (Autoscaler), Ethan Park (Control plane)
- SRE readiness: Rafael Mendes
- Exec sponsors (go/no-go): Priya Natarajan, Neha Kapoor

Notes / references
- This launch brief should stay aligned with the ADR on precedence + safety invariants and the Confluence PRD/design spec. If there is any mismatch, flag in #product-dedicated and update before external comms.
